action: If you run refrigeration or building controllers, take their management interfaces off the internet, change default passwords and apply vendor fixes. Keep a manual plan for moving stock if cooling fails.
exec: A physical-sabotage cyber campaign against food retail is now a diplomatic matter, with EU sanctions and arrest warrants being pursued.
impact: Retailers discarded spoiled stock; a November wave touched more than 100 sites across Europe, including French blood bank cold storage.
org: French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs
plain: France blames an Iranian military hacking unit for attacks that overheated supermarket fridges and freezers, and is asking the EU to sanction those responsible.

key_findings: In a November 10 interview published by the ministry, Jean-Noel Barrot called the refrigeration attack unprecedented in scale and aggressiveness and the first sabotage cyberattack of that size.
He said he would summon Iran's ambassador to convey France's protest.
He said France will seek EU sanctions on those responsible, meaning entry bans and asset freezes, as early as possible.
He said further proportionate measures would follow, some of which would not be made public.
He did not name the unit himself and declined to say whether Iran is behind other recent cyberattacks, citing ongoing investigations.
report.publisher: French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs
recommendations: The interview contains no guidance for organisations.

sources.name: French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs (France Info interview, 10 November 2026)

summary: Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said France will show EU foreign ministers in Brussels its evidence tying an IRGC cyber unit to the refrigeration-controller attacks and wants a sanctions list within a month. The campaign began October 11, hit about 700 French commercial sites and was linked to at least 15 fires. Paris prosecutors have requested international arrest warrants. Iran has routinely denied such operations.
title: France to seek EU sanctions on Iran's Revolutionary Guards over refrigeration sabotage

validation.note: Reviewed against the original French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs document, the minister's November 10 interview transcript. It confirms the push for EU sanctions and the summons of Iran's ambassador. The 700-site figure, the one-month target, the fires and the arrest warrants are not in it and rest on press coverage.
